summary: In more_itertools/more.py, rewrote the too_long branches of one() and only() so they raise too_long directly when `too_long is not None`, instead of `raise too_long or ValueError(msg)`, which swallowed falsy exception instances. The default ValueError message is now built inline only on the default path, so the f-string (which reprs the first two items) is never evaluated when a custom exception is supplied — this fixes items whose repr raises. In one(), the empty-iterable path similarly raises `too_short` when not None, else the unchanged default ValueError. Docstrings untouched. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_more.py` passed: 609 passed, 11313 subtests passed.
